t.E556.agn: In 2008, EFSA set a tolerable weekly intake (TWI) of 1 mg/kg body weight and reported that this limit may be exceeded in a significant part of the European population. The main sources are cereals, vegetables and beverages; the contribution of additives could not be quantified.
t.E556.body: Aluminium is very poorly absorbed from food (about 0.1%), but the absorbed part may accumulate in tissues, especially bone.
t.E556.eff.0.t: Aluminium from all sources may exceed the weekly limit; the absorbed part may accumulate in tissues. The contribution of additives could not be quantified
t.E556.eff.0.w: A significant part of the European population
t.E556.eval: It is no longer authorised as a food additive in the EU: its authorisation ended on 31 January 2014 under Regulation (EU) 380/2012 (review of aluminium-containing additives). In Türkiye, it is also not on the current permitted list of the Turkish Food Codex.
t.E556.prod: It is a chemically produced silicate.
t.E556.regx.0: Weekly limit for the whole diet of 1 mg/kg; may be exceeded in part of the population.
t.E556.summary: A silicate containing aluminium. It prevents caking of powdered products; it is used in salt, powdered sugar and spice blends.
t.E556.what: It prevents caking in powdered foods.
